world.title: Iran war: Trump says US in no hurry to end Iran conflict
world.summary: Donald Trump stated that the United States is not in a hurry to conclude its conflict with Iran, emphasizing that the financial burden of the military campaign is manageable. He noted that revenue from significant crude oil shipments from Venezuela has offset costs. His comments arise amid speculation about potential renewed military strikes against Tehran.

world.title: UK govt announces new ‘safe and legal’ routes for refugees in India to resettle in UK
world.summary: The UK government has introduced three new refugee resettlement routes for individuals in India and six other countries. These routes aim to provide "safe and legal" options for refugees, allowing sponsorship through charities, employers, and universities. This initiative seeks to deter asylum-seekers from dangerous journeys to the UK, such as crossing the English Channel in small boats.

world.title: PM-President face-off in Poland: Top court chief suspended, court cries 'coup d'etat' as Nawrocki returns
world.summary: Poland experienced heightened tensions as Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended the suspension of Chief Justice Malgorzata Nawrocki, who returned amid allegations of a "coup d'état" from the court. Riot police were deployed around the constitutional tribunal, reflecting the ongoing conflict between the government and nationalist factions. The situation escalated as President Andrzej Duda rushed back to address the crisis.

business.title: OpenAI slashes funding target by $10 billion amid tech rout, FT reports
business.summary: OpenAI has reduced its funding target for the latest round by $10 billion, according to a Financial Times report. This decision comes amid a significant selloff in technology stocks, largely attributed to concerns surrounding artificial intelligence. The adjustment reflects the current market conditions affecting tech companies, as investors reassess their positions in the wake of these developments.

business.title: Noel Tata seeks board scrutiny of SP Group's Rs 25,000 crore exit plan, Tata Sons restructuring
business.summary: Noel Tata has requested the Tata Sons board to review the Shapoorji Pallonji Group's Rs 25,000-crore funding proposal via capital reduction. He also urged the board to assess Tata Trusts' restructuring plan aimed at maintaining the holding company's unlisted status. Both matters are scheduled for discussion at the upcoming board meeting on November 26.

business.title: Rahul Gandhi vs Nirmala Sitharaman round 2, this time over IDBI Bank stake sale
business.summary: Rahul Gandhi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman engaged in a social media exchange regarding the government's decision to sell its stake in IDBI Bank. Gandhi supported the employees' strike against the sale, criticizing the government's actions. Sitharaman defended the decision, emphasizing its benefits. The dispute highlights ongoing tensions between the Congress party and the ruling government over economic policies.

technology.title: Microsoft killed Android apps on Windows 11, but they’re back in taskbar Search, streamed from your phone
technology.summary: Windows 11's taskbar Search now allows users to launch Android apps from their phones through the Phone Link feature. In a test, typing "Bluesky" in Search displayed the app installed on a Samsung phone as a “Mobile App” result. This functionality revives access to Android apps on Windows 11, which was previously removed.

technology.title: Windows 11 is full of web apps eating 1GB+ RAM because Microsoft neglected WinUI, and now it’s finally fixing it by adding basic features developers wanted
technology.summary: Microsoft is enhancing WinUI, the native framework for Windows 11, by introducing essential features like native TableView, Chart, and inking controls. These additions address developers' needs and aim to reduce reliance on Electron and web apps, which have been consuming over 1GB of RAM. The improvements are expected to benefit finance tools, admin panels, and note-taking applications.

technology.title: Trial By Error: Some Recent Observations from Alem Matthees
technology.summary: Alem Matthees has resumed communication after nearly a decade, marking a significant development in his field. On December 10, 2025, David Tuller received an email from Matthees, who has also expressed interest in sharing his insights and experiences. This renewed engagement could provide valuable perspectives on ongoing discussions and research within the community, highlighting Matthees' contributions.

sports.title: 'Not doing justice to their talent': Yuvraj Singh wants Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in ODIs
sports.summary: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh has expressed that young batters Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi should receive more opportunities in One Day Internationals (ODIs). He believes their talent is not being fully utilized in the current setup. Yuvraj's comments highlight the need for greater inclusion of emerging players in the national team for 50-over formats.

sports.title: ‘I did everything I could for India’: Poonam Raut on retirement and her unfinished comeback dream | Interview
sports.summary: Poonam Raut reflected on her four-year effort to return to the Indian cricket team, emphasizing her commitment through domestic performances and overcoming illness. Despite her dedication and scoring runs, she did not receive a call-up. Raut's last international match was in 2021, marking a challenging period as she pursued her dream of rejoining the national squad.

sports.title: F1 Mexico GP: Charles Leclerc pips McLaren and Mercedes to top FP2
sports.summary: Charles Leclerc secured the fastest time in the second practice session (FP2) at the Mexico Grand Prix, achieving a lap of 1m17.686s. He had previously topped the first session as well. McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell finished second and third, respectively. Leclerc's Ferrari teammate, Lewis Hamilton, retired from the session due to technical issues.

health.title: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000
health.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in over 5,000 deaths, according to government data released on Friday. This epidemic is the deadliest recorded in the country. Authorities continue to struggle with containment efforts, and there are currently no approved treatments available to combat the virus, exacerbating the public health crisis.

health.title: CMC observes World Stroke Day
health.summary: CMC Vellore celebrated World Stroke Day 2026 with various activities aimed at raising awareness about stroke care. The event featured screenings, multilingual discussions, survivor stories, and interactive reels. The theme for the day was "Each Minute Counts, Be FAST, Recognise Stroke, Save Lives." The observance took place on Friday at the CMC campus in Vellore and Ranipet.

health.title: Clinical professor discusses how to keep bones strong
health.summary: Emma Laing, a clinical professor and director of dietetics, discussed maintaining strong bones in an interview with health.com. She emphasized that inadequate sleep disrupts bone metabolism and increases osteoporosis risk. Laing highlighted the importance of adopting healthy lifestyle habits to support bone health, suggesting that foundational practices can significantly impact overall well-being and longevity in bone strength.

science.title: Ice Ejected Into Space; Ahmedabad Scientist Reveals
science.summary: Ahmedabad scientists have revealed that the Moon is gradually shrinking, a phenomenon that has puzzled researchers. Additionally, they reported the ejection of ice into space from the Moon. This discovery sheds light on the Moon's changing dynamics and its long-term relationship with Earth. The findings were discussed in an exclusive interview, highlighting ongoing research in lunar studies.

science.title: SEA STAR crew ends 5-day stay in Jules's Undersea Lab
science.summary: The SEA STAR crew has completed a five-day mission in Jules' Undersea Lab, located 22 feet underwater. During their stay, they faced the challenges of living under pressure while conducting research similar to space missions. The aquanauts studied the effects of pressure on cognitive functions and tested various underwater technologies before resurfacing to enjoy fresh air and sunlight.

science.title: Dinosaurs beginning with S: 10 fascinating prehistoric creatures you may not have heard of
science.summary: The article explores ten lesser-known dinosaurs that begin with the letter "S." It describes a vivid prehistoric scene, highlighting unique features such as long snouts with conical teeth and large tails. These fascinating creatures offer insights into the diversity of dinosaur life and their habitats, encouraging readers to learn more about these ancient animals and their environments.

entertainment.title: Horoscope Today: October 31, 2026
entertainment.summary: On October 31, 2026, Leos are advised to navigate a highly emotional period filled with resurfacing memories and nostalgia. While reflecting on past failures may evoke bittersweet feelings, it is emphasized that this is not the moment to dwell on sorrow. Instead, Leos are encouraged to focus on personal growth and embrace the present positively.

entertainment.title: Cody Rhodes apologizes for punting Randy Orton’s head off
entertainment.summary: Cody Rhodes apologized for delivering a punting move to Randy Orton's head during WrestleMania, sharing a graphic image of the resulting injury to Orton's face. He acknowledged the potential for a future retaliation from Orton, emphasizing the importance of respect in interactions with fans and contributors. The article also mentions community guidelines against trolling and disruptive behavior.

entertainment.title: Leo Horoscope Today: October 31, 2026
entertainment.summary: Today, Leos may experience heightened emotions and nostalgia, with memories of past failures resurfacing. While these feelings can be bittersweet, it is advised not to dwell on them or turn them into a sob story.
